# Captured analysis output

Raw `cargo aquascope permissions` stdout for fixtures in `../workspace/`, so that parsing and selection are tested without the toolchain. `05_method_mut_borrow`, `n1_non_ascii`, `e3_mod_other` and `e4_mixed_errors` are copied from spike 003's `work/results/noflag/`; `n2_nested` was captured the same way on 2026-11-06 (Aquascope v0.4.0, `nightly-2026-05-01`, edition 2024, library crate, no `--should-fail`). The `*.check.jsonl` files are the `cargo check --message-format=json` stdout for the same crates, copied from spike 003's `work/results/diagnostics/`, and feed the R10 classification tests. `n3_early_return` was captured the same way on 2026-11-08 with the pinned fork (`v0.4.0-vscode.1`, ADR 0004), and is kept as a sample of a result with boundaries but no steps: since `v0.4.0-vscode.7` (feature 010) the fork gives `Config::parse` its steps, so it is no longer what the current pin outputs for that file. For every other fixture the fork's output has the same content as v0.4.0's, so those captures still hold. Recapture them all if the pinned Aquascope version changes. They were captured before `v0.4.0-vscode.2`, so their results have no `file_path` (ADR 0004).

The `*.interp.json` files are raw `cargo aquascope interpreter` stdout for feature 007, captured on 2026-11-08 by `spikes/007-interpreter/probe.sh` (Aquascope v0.4.0, `nightly-2026-05-01`, edition 2024, binary crate, with a Miri-built standard library): `01_move_string`, `05_method_mut_borrow` and `n1_non_ascii` hold traces, `i4_use_after_free` a trace ending in undefined behaviour, and `i1_panic` the bare build error a runtime panic returns. `i6_no_main.check.jsonl` is the `cargo check` stdout for the program without `main` (E0601). Recapture them with that script if the pinned Aquascope version changes.

`crate/` holds feature 008's captures, written by `spikes/008-whole-crate/probe.sh` (T-044), and written again by T-049 on 2026-11-09 with the pinned fork (`v0.4.0-vscode.2`, `PROBE_INSTALL` set to spike 002's build), whose build errors also name their file (`--crate-of`, `file_path`). The probe replaces its own copy folder with `/copies` and the home folder with `~`, so the files hold no path of the machine that made them. `*.metadata.json` is `cargo metadata --no-deps --offline --format-version 1` in each fixture project, for finding a file's crate. `minigrep-config.json`, `workspace-app.json` and `minigrep-broken.json` are permissions output: a module of a split minigrep, a workspace member using another member, and the same minigrep with a compile error in `lib.rs`, whose `cargo check` output is `minigrep-broken.check.jsonl`. `*.stderr` is the run's error output for a dependency in no cache, a crates.io proc macro and a workspace proc macro with no linker, and a `build.rs`. Recapture them when the fork's output changes.

`stack-heap-crate/` holds feature 009's captures, written by `spikes/009-whole-crate-interpreter/probe.sh` (T-051) with its prototype of the fork, and checked by T-052 against the pinned fork (`v0.4.0-vscode.3`): minigrep's trace, its run with no arguments and the workspace's trace are byte for byte the same. The prototype's options were named `--allow-io` and `--main`; the fork's are `--disable-isolation` and `--bin-file`. Paths are normalised as in `crate/`.
